subject: PCA on entire clade or PCA on each subclade?

messages.author: c6308b8a6aace4ef
messages.subject: PCA on entire clade or PCA on each subclade?
parts: This might seem like an obvious question but here it goes. I want to compare the relative fit of different of models of trait evolution for each subclade in my phylogeny. To reduce the dimensionality of my high dimensional dataset before model fitting, I am wondering if it makes more sense to do a PCA for all the species in my tree and subset the resulting PC scores by subclade or do a PCA on each subclade prior to model fitting. I plan to use PC scores for model fitting.

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] PCA on entire clade or PCA on each subclade?
parts:
Nic,

for your new variables (ie PCs) to be commensurate, you need to run a single PCA, no matter what analysis you will then implement to them.

Just as a side note, some caution should be taken with fitting evolutionary models on PCs, see:

Uyeda JC, Caetano DS, Pennell MW. 2015 Comparative Analysis of Principal Components Can be Misleading. Syst. Biol. 64, 677–689. (doi:10.1093/sysbio/syv019)

Adams DC, Collyer ML. 2018 Multivariate Phylogenetic Comparative Methods : Evaluations , Comparisons , and Recommendations. Syst. Biol. 67, 14–31. (doi:10.1093/sysbio/syx055)

Adams DC, Collyer ML. 2019 Phylogenetic Comparative Methods and the Evolution of Multivariate Phenotypes. Annu. Rev. Ecol. Evol. Syst. 50, 405–425. (doi:10.1146/annurev-ecolsys-110218-024555)

Hope this helps

Antigoni
